children: most valuable competitive advantage may extend beyond its cars, racing heritage and global status, according to Morgan Stanley.
Analyst Edouard Aubin raised his price target on Ferrari by 4% to $460 while maintaining an Overweight rating. The new target represents approximately 15% upside from Wednesday's closing price.
Ferrari shares advanced Thursday following the report, putting the stock on course for its first positive session of the week.
Aubin's growing optimism rests on an element of Ferrari's brand that he believes investors often undervalue: the relationships created among its owners and collectors.

Luxury products traditionally deliver symbolic value through their associations with wealth, achievement and taste. Ferrari also offers an experiential benefit through the performance and emotion of driving one of its sports cars.
Aubin believes Ferrari adds two more layers. Its vehicles can retain investment appeal, while ownership provides access to a global community organized around the brand.
That fourth source of value has left the analyst increasingly positive about Ferrari demand over the coming years.

The company does more than sell cars to wealthy buyers. It provides events and experiences that allow customers to interact with other owners, deepen their relationship with Ferrari and potentially become repeat purchasers or collectors.

CEO Benedetto Vigna has expanded that engagement strategy since taking the top job in 2021. Ferrari has increased regional road and track activities and launched Ferrari Sport Prototipi Clienti for owners of the 499P Modificata.

The automaker is also bringing product introductions, motorsports, lifestyle experiences and hospitality together at individual events. Morgan Stanley views that platform as a structured tool for managing the entire customer relationship, helping Ferrari deepen loyalty without weakening its exclusivity.

That distinction matters for investors because Ferrari's growth depends not only on attracting new customers but also on encouraging existing clients to build larger collections. A strong owner community could reinforce demand while making the brand more difficult for other luxury automakers to replicate.
Analyst sentiment remains broadly favorable. Wall Street carries a Strong Buy consensus on Ferrari, while Seeking Alpha analysts rate the shares a Buy.

Morgan Stanley's revised target suggests Ferrari's investment case is not simply about selling more expensive sports cars. It is about turning ownership into a long-term relationship that supports loyalty, repeat purchases and durable demand.

title: Morgan Stanley Revamps Ferrari Stock Target on Overlooked Asset
